blocks.value: Communications Engineering courses basically teaches the basics of networking and communication to the students. Some of the core Communications Engineering subjects are digital circuits, electric signals, wave propagation, antenna design, computer networks etc.

The basic Communications Engineering eligibility criteria is to clear Class 12 with PCM subjects and secure minimum 50 to 60 percent marks. The admission for Communications Engineering is given on both merit and entrance basis. Students who wish to study Communications Engineering can prepare for entrance exams like GATE, AP PGECET, JEE Main , Karnataka PGECET, TNEA Counselling, and CUET PG.

Some well known Communications Engineering colleges in India are Jadavpur University, BITS Pilani, SOA University, SASTRA University, etc. The avg. Communications Engineering fees is approx. from INR 1 lakh to INR 6 lakh.

The popular Communications Engineering jobs in India include Telecom Caretaker, R&D Engineer, Test Engineer, and Electrical Engineer. Candidates completing this course get a chance to work with companies like DRDO, BSNL, Bharat Electronics Limited, Hindustan Aeronautics Limited, etc. The average Communications Engineering salary is INR 4 LPA to INR 6 LPA.

faqs.question: What is Communications Engineering?
faqs.answer: Communication Engineering designs and builds systems that connect us like mobiles, internet, radio and also satellites. It focuses on getting information using signals. It's about making sure your texts, calls and data reach their destination and covering everything from fiber optics to Wi-Fi.

faqs.question: What is the duration of Communications Engineering courses?
faqs.answer: Course duration of Communications Engineering courses varies on basis of course level. For UG Communications Engineering courses, duration in India is 4 years in general. For PG courses, duration is 2 years . If you want to enter work field at earliest, you can also go for a Diploma in Communications Engineering right after completing your Class 10, which is 3 years long. Furthermore, a PhD course in Communications Engineering can be 3 years to 6 years long , depending on your research topic and institution offering doctorate program. Most of colleges offer courses in this field at PG level, after you complete a bachelor's degree in ECE, EE, or a related field.

blocks.value: If a student is planning to have a career in Communications Engineering, he/she must pursue an undergraduate engineering program (BTech) after completion of which students can opt for a job or for a postgraduation program in the same stream. Primarily, Communication Engineering is offered as a specialization at the PG level at most of the popular colleges in India:

value: Students must pass Class 10 with Science and Mathematics subjects and a decent passing percentage of at least 50% marks.

Students must have passed the class 12 exam or equivalent and secured a minimum of 50 percent aggregate marks. They must have studied Physics, Chemistry, and Mathematics as core subjects. Students belonging to the reserved category are provided with a certain relaxation in minimum aggregate scores.

Students must hold a bachelor's degree in the field of Communication Engineering/Electronics and Communication Engineering or any other related field. The marks obtained during graduation should be at least between 55% marks. The admission to MTech in Communications Engineering is based on marks obtained in the entrance exam combined with performance in personal interview/group discussion based on the college/university.
Candidates must have completed MTech from a recognised university with a minimum of 55 percent marks. Must have cleared the Research Entrance Test for PhD scholars.

faqs.question: What is the eligibility for Communications Engineering?
faqs.answer: Hi, Eligibility for Communications Engineering varies depending on level of study: Undergraduate (B.Tech/B.E): Pass Class 12 with Physics, Chemistry, and Mathematics and score well in entrance exams like JEE Mains. Postgraduate (M.Tech): Bachelor's degree in Engineering (preferably ECE or related) with a minimum aggregate score (often 60%). Selection is based on entrance exams and sometimes interviews. Hope this helps !!

faqs.question: How can I get admission to M.Tech Communications Engineering at the IITs?
faqs.answer: In order to get admission to M.Tech in Communications Engineering course at IITs, you must meet minimum eligibility requirements. You should have at least 60% marks in your bachelor's degree in a relevant field . For reserved category candidates, marks eligibility requirement is usually relaxed by 5%. Further, you have to appear for GATE exam . You must secure a good rank in entrance exam as it plays most important role in admission process. After you successfully secure a decent rank in GATE, you will have to appear for COAP counselling process where you will be allotted a seat according to your rank at one of IIT branches in India. Often, there is also a written test or interview round after GATE results are announced. Interestingly, if you are an IIT BTech graduate with a CGPA of 8 or above, you need not give entrance test and are eligible for direct admission to course.

faqs.question: How are Communications Engineering courses typically taught?
faqs.answer: A combination of lectures, tutorials, laboratory sessions and also projects is common. Lectures introduce theoretical concepts, tutorials provide space for solving problems and applications, labs offer hands on experience with equipment and software and projects allow students to apply their knowledge to design and implement communication systems. There are a lot of core and elective subjects in Communications Engineering courses. Some general subjects are Signal Theory, Optical Switching and Networking, Communication Security, System Optimization and Data Transfer.

faqs.question: What are the core subjects taught in Communications Engineering classes?
faqs.answer: Communication Engineering syllabus covered in classes incorporates core subject areas, popular electives, hands-on training via lab work, and projects. general core subjects taught in Communications Engg. classes are given here: · Basic Electrical and Electronics Engineering · Semiconductor Physics · Introduction to Digital Systems and Fabrication · Signals and Systems · Network Analysis and Synthesis · Electromagnetic Field Theory · Antenna and Wave Propagation · Microwave Engineering · Digital Signal Processing · Wireless Communication

salary.title: Communications Engineering Career Scope, Job Profiles, Top Recruiters & Salary

blocks.value: Communications Engineering offers opportunities in large numbers in the Communications sector, including, radio, television, telephone, mobile communication, computers, etc. Candidates who have completed Communications Engineering can pursue the following job profiles:

value: Microwaves are created and used for communication by microwave engineers. They work on tasks like designing microwave circuits, creating new microwave technologies, and testing microwave equipment.
Telephone networks, the internet, and satellite communication are just a few examples of the telecommunications systems that telecommunications engineers develop, set up, and maintain.
Signal analysis and processing engineers work with information-carrying signals.
Antenna engineers design and analyze antennas, which are used to transmit and receive radio waves.

faqs.question: Is pursuing Communications Engineering worth it?

blocks.value: Whether it is smart homes, rover technology or IoT communication technology is in all fields from healthcare to transportation systems to avionics. Future is all around connectivity and transmitting and receiving information through signal processing. Whether one is using their phone, turning on radio or strumming their electric guitar they are sending and receiving signals all time. That's why you won't regret pursuing a major degree course in this field.

faqs.question: Are there any specializations offered in Communications Engineering courses?

blocks.value: Communications Engineering is a part of Electrical Engineering discipline which basically deals with planning, building and up keeping of systems for transferring and receiving information. This includes wired and wireless communication systems like radio, television, telephone networks and also internet technology. Talking about areas of specialization many programs do offer specializations in topics like wireless communication (cellular networks, satellite communication), optical communication (fiber optic systems), communication network engineering, information theory and coding and even communication system security. You get a lot of options to explore and experiment with.
